items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: Shep appreciated Louis, you know. Um, he could, Shep wasn't the kind of a guy that would have thought of Louis as a commercial asset for the city. But he was just happy that he was from here.

ctx.x: I was to his house in Long Island with Bobby Hackett. And we talked about it then. He said, those people there, he said, I don't know what's the matter with them. But he said, but I wouldn't go back there anymore. Those are awful people. Yeah. So that was it.
When Louis came back at Zulu, Mayor Morrison gave him Keys to the City. Sure. I mean, the thing is. How do you think Morrison viewed Louis? I mean, what was his?

Oh, well, he considered him to be a great delight and that he was a big asset to the city, the fact that Louis was from here. I mean, Shep appreciated Louis, you know. Um, he could, Shep wasn't the kind of a guy that would have thought of Louis as a commercial asset for the city. But he was just happy that he was from here.
